clue.text: Flag up puzzle feature on the perimeter — snails

indicators.note: the puzzle feature sits all round the outside of the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a nina is a hidden message a setter plants in a crossword grid

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flag, a puzzle feature and a perimeter, then mentions snails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun, a banner, but it is the verb meaning to weaken. 'up' reverses it in this down clue, and 'on the perimeter' wraps the crossword feature round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neritina is a genus of small freshwater and coastal snails, so the answer names those molluscs.

clue.text: Being obsequious to American on the way out

parts.note: something on the way out is dying

explanation.surface: A sycophant fawns over an American who is about to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadying is fawning, servile flattery, which is the behaviour of an obsequious person.

clue.text: Schools doctor withdrawing complaints

indicators.note: the doctor pulls out of the longer word, leaving what remains

parts.note: to school someone is to train or drill them

explanation.surface: A school doctor is pulled out, leaving the pupils with their complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schools' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in trains or DRILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills and complaints are both ailments or illnesses, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Crowning achievement — emptied flipping chamberpot

indicators.note: a word that is emptied loses all its inside letters and keeps only its two ends
flipping turns this short word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a po is British slang for a chamberpot

explanation.surface: A mock-heroic boast about tipping out a chamberpot as one's crowning achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps A and T of achievement; 'flipping' turns PO, a British word for a chamberpot, into OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crowning another sits on top of it, which is what atop means.

clue.text: Member initially gets in two beers — barman here one of the best

definitions.text: barman here one of the best

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: the letter from gets is placed inside the beers

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, so two beers are ale and ale

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word gets

explanation.surface: A club member orders two beers and the barman is praised as one of the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The barman is not a pub worker but a member of the Bar, a barrister; 'here' tells you to read him so.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal eagle is a sharp, highly capable lawyer, the pick of the barristers.

clue.text: Lord's tenants having relations evicted — that's mean

indicators.note: the relations are thrown out of the longer word, as tenants might be

parts.note: Middlesex County Cricket Club play their home games at Lord's, which they rent
sexual relations, or sex

explanation.surface: A landlord throws out tenants whose relatives moved in, which seems mean.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, home of Middlesex, a county side; 'Lord's tenants' is not about a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of values is its average, the middle value.

clue.text: British ship has space on board

indicators.note: in a down clue the space sits on top of the British ship

parts.note: an em is a printer's space, the width of the letter M
Noah's ark is the classic ship

explanation.surface: A British vessel turns out to have room for passengers on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like one phrase, but 'on' places EM above, and 'board' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or other vessel, which is to board it.

clue.text: One lot (nameless) trained with RAF fliers

indicators.note: the letters are drilled into a new formation, so rearranged
losing the name means dropping N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A batch of people, unnamed, has been trained alongside Royal Air Force pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' strips N from ONE LOT, leaving OELOT, and 'trained' mixes that with RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeroflot is the Russian national airline, so its aircraft and crews are fliers.

clue.text: Puzzle's meaning not essentially obscure

indicators.note: the remaining letters are obscured, jumbled out of their order
the essential, central letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzle's meaning is said to be not really obscure at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not essentially' removes the middle letter N of MEANING, leaving MEAING for 'obscure' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling that must be worked out.

clue.text: Accents of Dutch wearing dated hats

indicators.note: the Dutch letter is worn inside the hats, surrounded by them

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Dutch people are pictured in old-fashioned headwear, with their accents noted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy diacritic mark placed over letters such as the Spanish n.

clue.text: Plan raid after serving of meal

indicators.note: the letters are served up in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Raiders plot their attack once the meal has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' hints at postprandial but is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Prandial is an adjective describing things relating to a dinner or lunch.

clue.text: Disturbing conundrum ultimately leaves cabinet chasing its tail

indicators.note: the final letter runs round to the front, like a dog after its tail
the chosen letter departs from the word for the cabinet

parts.note: the cabinet is made up of ministers

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of conundrum

explanation.surface: A government cabinet, baffled by a riddle, spins in circles, which is disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops M from MINISTERS, giving INISTERS; 'chasing its tail' moves the final S to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinister is ominous or menacing, so it is disturbing to witness.

clue.text: Beats arrangement from Wet Wet Wet we always dismissed?

parts.words: from Wet Wet Wet we always dismissed
parts.note: taking WE out of each Wet leaves three Ts in a row, and T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pop fan suggests a song arrangement that leaves the band Wet Wet Wet out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Wet Wet Wet were a Scottish pop band. Remove 'we' each time and only T T T is left: three Ts, with T the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple time is a musical metre with three beats to the bar, an arrangement of beats.

clue.text: Are inside keeping some measure of control

indicators.note: the two words hold some of their letters together as the answer

explanation.surface: Something inside is said to keep a partial grip on events.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps a rider uses to steer a horse, hence a means of control.

clue.text: First lady back home welcoming a thousand people from Siberia

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: the reversed home lets the thousand in, enclosing it
back means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home
K is short for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A president's wife, home again, welcomes a thousand visitors from Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IN into NI, and 'welcoming' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Evenki are an indigenous Tungusic people of Siberia and northern China.

clue.text: Possible concessions — getting into pub grub

indicators.note: the word for getting goes into the pub grub, between the two parts

parts.note: a bar is a pub
grub is food, here chips
getting means gaining

explanation.surface: Pub food is offered as a possible concession during tough talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips here are British chips, fried potato fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargaining chips are things offered up or traded away in negotiation, as concessions.

clue.text: Perennial scheme which involves cycling

indicators.note: letters at the end are cycled round to the front

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
that can mean which, as a relative pronoun

explanation.surface: A long-running scheme is said to involve cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves cycling' moves HAT from the end of PLANTHAT round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The hat plant is a flowering shrub that lives for many years, a perennial.

clue.text: Periods I spent in fort

indicators.note: the letters are spent, used up and broken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the time periods they spent stationed in a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A presidio is a fortified military post, particularly one built by the Spanish in the Americas.

clue.text: Sad way of working out what container may hold?

indicators.note: the way of working is taken out of the sad word

parts.note: mournful means sad
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A sorrowful method of solving a problem is described.
explanation.definitionFit: An urnful is the quantity an urn holds, an urn being a vase-like container.

clue.text: Put up again outside hotel — anger misplaced

indicators.note: the mixed-up anger sits outside the hotel letter, enclosing it
the letters are put in the wrong places, rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A guest outside a hotel is furious about something hung up in the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges ANGER as REANG, and 'outside' places it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehang a picture or curtain is to hang it again, putting it back up.

clue.text: Though upset, call for dismissal

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so backwards

parts.note: if can mean though, as in odd if not wrong
to give someone a ring is to call them

explanation.surface: Though upset, someone calls for another to be sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing someone is sacking them, ending their employment, which is dismissal.

clue.text: Played tapes to entertain little one in bed

indicators.note: the shuffled tapes take the small word in, as a host entertains a guest
the letters are played about with, rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Tapes are played to amuse a small child tucked up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little one' reads as a child, but 'one' starts the definition: a bed here is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a fragrant climbing flower commonly grown in a garden bed.

clue.text: Hotel chain delayed taking action over that woman inside

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the phrase for delay

parts.note: to sit on something is to put off acting on it
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A hotel company dragged its feet over a matter involving a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' is not the NATO letter H here; the whole phrase 'Hotel chain' is the definition. 'inside' places the pronoun within the phrase for putting off action.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheraton is an international brand of hotels, part of the Marriott group.

clue.text: Animal rescuer not finishing early — that's good

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter, cut short

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of satisfaction

explanation.surface: An animal rescuer who doesn't finish early is praised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Noah built the ark and saved the animals two by two from the flood.

clue.text: Old scorer (as Peter Crouch is)

parts.note: Peter Crouch, the former England striker, is famously very tall

explanation.surface: A footballer, the striker Peter Crouch, is called an old goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a footballer, but it means a composer who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was a sixteenth-century English composer, so a writer of musical scores long ago.

clue.text: Mineral — type I twice rejected

indicators.note: the letters named are rejected, thrown out of the type word

parts.note: italic is a style of type

indicators.note: the letter I is to be taken out two times

explanation.surface: A mineral sample of one type was turned down on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Is go from ITALIC, leaving TALC.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, hydrated magnesium silicate, ground to make talcum powder.

clue.text: Shortly the setter's retiring — one won't reveal his identity

parts.note: anon means soon, shortly

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: my is the setter's word for their own

explanation.surface: The crossword setter soon retires, keeping their identity secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns MY into YM.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is a person who stays anonymous, or a pseudonym used to stay unnamed.

clue.text: A lot of water in room upstairs — get daughter out

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes in the room upstairs

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house

indicators.note: the daughter is let out of the word for get

parts.note: to land something is to get it

explanation.surface: Water floods the attic, and a daughter must be fetched out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes D from LAND to give LAN, which goes 'in' ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is an ocean, an immense body of sea water.
